title: Closure under negation and identification
statement: For all natural numbers $n,m$, if $f$ is a $\pm 1$-valued linear threshold function on $\{0,1\}^n$, then for every $z\in\{0,1\}^n$ and every map $\pi:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, the function $g:\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb R$ defined by $g(w)=f((z_i+w_{\pi(i)}\bmod 2)_{i=0}^{n-1})$ is a $\pm 1$-valued linear threshold function.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ belongs to the linear threshold class on dimension $n$
coordinate map $\pi$ from the $n$ input coordinates to the $m$ coordinates
replaced:
For all $n,m\in\mathbb N$, real coefficients $c,a_1,\ldots,a_n$, $z\in\{0,1\}^{n}$ and maps $\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{1,\ldots,m\}$, if $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(c+\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i(-1)^{x_i})$, then $g(w)=f((z_i+w_{\pi(i)}\pmod2)_{i=1}^{n})$ is a $\{-1,1\}$-valued linear threshold function on $\{0,1\}^{m}$, meaning that $g(w)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(b+\sum_{j=1}^{m}u_j(-1)^{w_j})$ for some real $b,u_1,\ldots,u_m$.
Here $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
